column3: 1. I had a set morning routine on school days (i.e., I usually did the same thing each day to get ready).
column4: 2. My parents were often late to pick me up (e.g. from school, aftercare or sports).
column5: 4. My family ate a meal together most days.
column6: 3. My parents kept track of what I ate (e.g., made sure that I didn’t skip meals or tried to make sure I ate healthy food).
column7: 5. My parents tried to make sure I got a good night's sleep (e.g., I had a regular bed time, my parents checked to make sure I went to sleep).
column8: 6. I had a bedtime routine (e.g., my parents tucked me in, my parents read me a book, I took a bath).
column9: 7. In my after school or free time hours at least one of my parents knew what I was doing.
column10: 8. I usually knew when my parents were going to be home.
column11: 9. At least one of my parents regularly checked that I did my homework.
column12: 10. At least one of my parents regularly kept track of my school progress.
column13: 11. At least one of my parents had punishments that were unpredictable.
column14: 12. I often wondered whether or not one of my parents would come home at the end of the day.
column15: 13. There were often people coming and going in my house that I did not expect to be there.
column16: 14. At least one parent made time each day to see how I was doing.
column17: 15. My family planned activities to do together
column18: 16. At least one of my parents would plan something for the family, but then not follow through with the plan.
column19: 17. My family had holiday traditions that we did every year (e.g.,cooking a special food at a particular time of year/decorate the house the same way).
column20: 18. There was a long period of time when I didn’t see one of my parents (e.g. military deployment, jail time, custody arrangements).
column21: 19. I experienced changes in my custody arrangement.
column23: 21. At least one of my parents changed jobs frequently.
column24: 22. There were times when one of my parents was unemployed and couldn’t find a job even though he/she wanted one.
column25: 23. There was a period of time when I often worried that I was not going to have enough food to eat.
column26: 24. There was a period of time when I often worried that my family would not have enough money to pay for necessities like clothing or bills.
column27: 25. There was a period of time when I did not feel safe in my home.
column30: 28. My parents had a stable relationship with each other.
column32: 30. At least one of my parents had many romantic partners.
column33: 31. At least one of my parents was disorganized.
column34: 32. At least one of my parents was unpredictable.
column35: 33. For at least one of my parents, when they were upset I did not know how they would act.
column36: 34. One of my parents could go from calm to furious in an instant.
column37: 35. One of my parents could go from calm to stressed or nervous in an instant.
column38: 37. I lived in a cluttered house (e.g., piles of stuff everywhere).
column39: 38. In my house things I needed were often misplaced so that I could not find them.
column40: 36. I lived in a clean house.
